The command keeps running after this call returns and after the caller's
connection drops: erun gives it its own session and captures its merged
stdout and stderr to the job's log, so nothing has to be wrapped in setsid,
nohup, or a redirect.

The exit status is recorded by the process that waits on the work, inside
the environment, so no sentinel token and no shell expansion sit between the
work and its result. The id defaults to the name; re-using the id of a job
that is still running is refused, while re-using a finished one replaces it.

--agent runs an AI tool instead of a command, with the trailing arguments as
the prompt. erun invokes the tool in its streaming mode, which is what makes
an agent run observable at all: left to its default the tool prints nothing
until it exits, so a multi-hour run reports no output while it is actively
editing files. status then reports the current activity, not only "running".
This is a one-shot, non-interactive run: nothing wakes it once it exits, so
the prompt must not end its own turn believing something will notify it
about work it is still waiting on -- there is no such notification, with one
narrow exception. If this job's own process ends while a job it started has
not reached a verdict, or has reached a bad one, erun resumes the same
session with the concrete outcome so the agent can act on it -- fix it,
verify it, or explain why it cannot be resolved. This is bounded (a small
fixed count and a wall-clock budget, both shown by `job status` as
"resumed N/M") and applies only to that one narrow case, never to a plain
failing exit code: past the bound, or for any other outcome, there is still
no notification and no further "later".

--env sets additional environment for the job's own process, on top of what
it inherits from the environment's runtime pod — for example raising
CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS for one agent run. Values land in the job
supervisor's argv, visible to anything that can list processes in this
environment, so this is not where secrets belong; PATH, LD_PRELOAD, and a
few other names that could redirect what the job executes are refused.

When this start itself runs from inside another job's own work (an agent
job running `job start` for a gate, the common case), that other job waits
for this one to reach a verdict before it reports its own outcome — its exit
code alone is never trusted while work it started has not finished. Pass
--handoff for work that is meant to outlive the caller on purpose (a release,
a long render): it excludes this job from that wait entirely.

--exclusive declares that the work needs the environment to itself. While it
runs, every other job start here is refused and told which job holds the
environment, rather than being queued or quietly allowed to contend. That
includes plain jobs, not only other --exclusive ones: a gate needs protecting
less from another gate than from everything else scheduled beside it. Reach
for it whenever the work saturates the environment and a neighbour would make
its result meaningless -- a full gate run measured 7 minutes alone and 17
minutes with a second batch beside it, going red on two tests that pass
standalone. The claim is a lease, not a lock: it expires without renewal and
is reclaimed once its holder's process is gone, so a crashed job cannot pin
the environment. Work this job itself starts is exempt -- a nested job runs
under this claim instead of being refused by it.

Usage:
  erun job start [flags] -- <command> [args...]

Examples:
  # Start a test suite and come back for the result.
  erun exec job start --tenant team --environment dev --name suite -- ./gradlew test
  erun exec job await --tenant team --environment dev --id suite --timeout 5m

  # Start an agent and watch what it is doing.
  erun exec job start --tenant team --environment dev --name sweep --agent claude -- 'fix the failing tests'
  erun exec job status --tenant team --environment dev --id sweep

  # Raise an agent's output-token cap for this run only.
  erun exec job start --tenant team --environment dev --name sweep --agent claude \
    --env CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS=64000 -- 'rewrite the module'

  # Kick off a release that is meant to keep running past this run's own turn.
  erun exec job start --tenant team --environment dev --name release --handoff -- erun release

  # Run a gate that must not share the environment with anything else.
  erun exec job start --tenant team --environment dev --name check --exclusive -- make check-gate

Flags:
      --agent string           Run an AI tool (claude or codex) in streaming mode, taking the trailing arguments as its prompt
      --dir string             Working directory in the environment to run the command from
      --dry-run                Resolve and trace mutating actions without executing them.
      --env stringArray        Additional KEY=VALUE environment for the job's process; repeat for several. Not for secrets: values are visible in the job supervisor's argv
      --environment string     Environment the job runs in
      --exclusive              Claim the environment for this job's lifetime; while it is held, every other job start here is refused and told which job holds it
      --handoff                Mark this job as deliberately meant to outlive whatever starts it, excluding it from that job's own finish check
  -h, --help                   help for start
      --id string              Handle to address the job by (defaults to the name)
      --lease-ttl duration     Activity lease TTL the job renews inside while it runs (default 15m0s)
      --max-output-bytes int   Cap on captured output; past it output is dropped and the job says so (default 16777216)
      --name string            What the work is, shown wherever the environment reports as busy
      --tenant string          Tenant whose environment the job belongs to

Global Flags:
      --output string   Result format: text (default, human stream) or json (structured result on stdout for orchestrators). (default "text")
      --time            Print the elapsed runtime after the command finishes.
  -v, --verbose count   Increase verbosity: -v streams external tool output, -vv adds erun command traces.
